- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model underestimates; adjust upward by 3–7% to reflect risk reversal or market panic.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply smoothing filter or lag 1–2 days to dampen overshoot.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model often fails to catch the momentum; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% per day of sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; add 1–2% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is rising.
- If sentiment is flat or neutral (0.0–0.4), model tends to drift downward; apply upward bias of 1–3% to avoid “sitting on the floor”.
- Overshoot after spikes: if price spikes >10% from prior high, model often forecasts 10–20% above true; cap forecast at +5% above prior high.
